findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in the rules list
findings.body: In FilterViewResults, the 'grafana' switch branch renders <GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={...} ... /> without passing the `key` prop. The old <GrafanaRuleLoader> had `key={key}`, and the sibling branches ('datasource' and the default) still pass `key={key}`. The KeyedRuleWithOrigin type comment explicitly states the artificial key exists 'to prevent key duplication' in the rule list. Without a key, React falls back to index-based reconciliation, which can misassociate state (e.g. open dropdowns, drawers) with the wrong rule when items are added/removed during infinite scroll or polling, and produces duplicate-index warnings. Pass `key={key}` to GrafanaRuleListItem.

findings.title: Silence notifications menu item does nothing in the new Grafana rule list
findings.body: The 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown whenever `canSilence` is true, and `canSilence` can now be satisfied purely via the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` path (which only needs the prom rule). However, the drawer that the click handler opens is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, where `rule` is the ruler rule. In the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons) no ruler rule is passed, so `rule` is undefined, the condition is always false, and the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never renders. Users with silence permission see the menu item, click it, and nothing happens. Either pass the prom rule to the drawer or gate the menu item on the drawer actually being openable.

findings.title: Delete (and Pause) menu items can never render in the ruler-less list view despite abilities being computed for them
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu now computes `canDelete` (and `canPause`) as an OR of the ruler-rule ability and the new grafana prom-rule ability, specifically so the menu works in the alert list view where no ruler rule is fetched. But the render conditions still require the ruler rule: the Delete item is `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}` (line 165) and the Pause item is `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...}` (line 123). Since RuleActionsButtons passes `rulerRule={rule}` with `rule === undefined` in the new list, Delete and Pause silently disappear from the list view even for users with AlertingRuleDelete/Update permissions — a regression from the previous list where ruler rules were fetched and these actions were available. The grafana-based canDelete/canPause computations are dead code as rendered. Either remove the rulerRule gate and make the handlers work from the prom-rule identifier, or drop the grafana ability path for these actions.

findings.title: Test codifies the missing Delete action instead of catching the regression
findings.body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' grants AlertingRuleDelete (and AlertingRuleUpdate) permissions via grantUserPermissions and setFolderAccessControl, yet asserts `menuItems.length` is exactly 4 (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) with no Delete item. This locks in the regression where Delete (and Pause) are unreachable in the ruler-less list view, and the comment 'all 4 menu actions should be available' contradicts the granted permissions. The test should assert that Delete is present when the user has delete permission, and there is no test covering clicking 'Silence notifications' (which would reveal the drawer never opens) or the pause action.

findings.title: Removed ruler reconciliation drops transient Creating/Deleting states
findings.body: GrafanaGroupLoader previously merged the Prometheus and Ruler group responses: ruler-only rules (just created, not yet propagated to Prometheus) rendered as 'Creating', and prom-only rules (deleted in the ruler, not yet propagated) rendered as a read-only 'Deleting' item. Now only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` is rendered. Consequences: (1) a newly created rule is invisible in the list until Prometheus propagation completes, with no feedback; (2) a rule the user just deleted still renders as a fully normal, active list item with an Edit button (and copy-link/export) that operate on a rule that no longer exists in the ruler, producing failing actions and confusion. If eventual consistency is now guaranteed, that should be validated; otherwise the eventual-consistency handling needs to be preserved.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries returnTo, breaking back-navigation to the list
findings.body: The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader/GrafanaRuleListItem built the rule href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating to the rule view preserved the list context for the back/return navigation. The new GrafanaRuleListItem (line 40) builds `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no returnTo. Users who click a rule in the filtered list and then try to go back lose their filter/search context. If this was intentional it should be noted; otherwise restore the returnTo parameter.
